newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia seeks to delay becoming net oil importer.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia seeks to delay becoming net oil importer.

text.p: Indonesia, Asia's only OPEC member, will do its best to postpone becoming a net oil importer, President Suharto said on Tuesday.

"On account of the possibilities of exploiting the potential oil/gas and geothermal reserves at our disposal, we shall try our best to postpone as long as possible the time when our country will become a net importer of oil," he said.
Suharto was addressing the 25th annual convention of the Indonesian Petroleum Association.
He said efforts were being made to discover new oil and gas and geothermal deposits.
"Similar efforts are being conducted to make the most efficient use of oil and gas and to diversify the use of energy."
Indonesia currently produces about 1.60 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil and condensate and exports 760,000 bpd of crude.
Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita said in August that with rising domestic demand, the country could become a net oil importer by 2005 if new reserves were not discovered.
Suharto said Indonesia was trying to create a better investment climate to encourage investment.

"Furthermore (state oil company) Pertamina can also expand the basis of its oil/gas resources -- if necessary beyond Indonesia -- with a view to raising and securing oil supply, as well as increasing foreign exchange revenues," he said.

"Well aware that such a venture requires a huge capital, we shall continue to offer the opportunity to both foreign and local partners to work together with Pertamina in the oil and gas industry in Indonesia," Suharto added.
He said it was essential to secure markets and capture new markets. At the same time, efforts had to be made to lower production costs through increased efficiency, effectiveness and productivity.

"Pertamina and its partners have made encouraging progress. However, further restructuring and improvement, both internally and externally, are still needed to make Pertamina self-reliant and to have the potential to compete with international oil and natural gas companies," Suharto said.
